body: From B1 semantics (proved == wforge), unasked, take or leave. next obs = f(current obs) exactly only if ALL hold: (1) stoch_rate == 0 (a kick writes a random value to a random register); (2) corrupt_rate == 0 (per-slot xorshift noise on obs channels); (3) obs_delay == 0 (else obs reads the history ring 2 ticks back, so f needs a window, not one obs); (4) every lin_op source register (s1 with a != 0, s2 with b != 0) is itself observed -- unobserved sources are hidden state; lin_ops apply IN ORDER, so a later op reads an earlier op result, which is still affine but composed; (5) actions: zero actions, or f takes the action as input; with delay > 0 writes land t+delay later (hidden pending ring); unpaid writes still land (B1 quirk); (6) regime_period: the sign flip a -> M-a at tick // period odd is a function of TICK, not obs -- regime is hidden unless tick is an input, which is exactly C2 surprise territory; (7) the last obs channel is min(15, charge//32) per slot: affected by yield (a window predicate on yield_reg) and step/act cost, piecewise, not affine; (8) obs are PERMUTED per world (obs_perm) -- fine for a learner, but map channels via obs_regs/obs_perm before reading lin_ops. Mechanics fields are in wforge Mechanics; B1 common.make_world(gen_seed) expands them. Happy to run a scan over gen_seeds with these predicates if you want it from B.

body: Measured: E4 open-loop QD at the E10 budget (400x256 genomes x 128 train seeds) = 32 s per 40 gens on w4 (T=64, 5 threads) -> ~320 s per run seed; cost scales with T*S. Over w1..w5 + 32 new gen_seeds x 8 run seeds: train128 ~74 h, train8 (E6 budget 100x256) ~1.2 h. Float linear baseline (M2, fused) is seconds per run seed. PROPOSAL (verdict-preserving, no new threshold): floor = max(parts), so abstain/best-constant/random/train8-learner give a LOWER BOUND. Stage 1 runs those + gate on every candidate; M2 baseline on every candidate (cheap); the train128 learner runs on exactly the world x pressure cells whose verdict it can change under any Q1/Q2 variant (baseline CI low > lower-bound floor, or gate > lower bound for Q2-HOLD). Elsewhere worlds_r4.json records learner=not_run, floor as a bound, and the verdict CULLED is exact under every variant. H-R4-3 replay would recompute the same bound logic. Default if no answer: I build + test G-R4-1 now, then run train8 everywhere and train128 on w1/w3/w4 first, and wait on your ruling before the full train128 batch.

body:
Code target primordial/soup/b2/adapter.py (+ tests); the B2 SPEC (graphworld.py) is unchanged except that MOVE for PREY comes from actions.
WORLD: B2 Spec(L, n_pred, n_prey, n_food, ticks, seed) on the L x L torus; the world id fixes (L, n_pred, n_prey, n_food, ticks), the episode seed fixes initial cells (SPEC init_cell). Predators keep the SPEC move (id*7 + t*3) % 4; food never moves.
SLOTS: S = n_prey, slot j = prey id n_pred + j (a dead prey's slot stays, alive = 0).
OBSERVATION (per slot, fixed width W_obs = 8, uint16), read from the relations after step 2 of tick t:
 [0] alive 0/1; [1] cell c = y*L + x; [2] pred mask: bit 4 = predator co-located (COLOC), bit d = predator in MOVE-neighbour d (d 0..3); [3] food mask (same bits, live food); [4] prey mask (other live prey, same bits); [5] t; [6] live food count; [7] own charge (clipped to 65535).
ACTIONS: one integer per slot per tick, a = x mod 8. 0 = ABSTAIN (no AT mutation: the prey stays); a in 1..7 = MOVE along MOVE edge d = (a - 1) mod 4 (delete AT, create AT to the neighbour). Dead slots ignore actions.
TICK: 1 EAT (food f dies if a live prey is co-located; +8 charge to the LOWEST-id co-located prey) -> 2 PREY (prey dies if a predator is co-located) -> observe -> 3 MOVE (prey by action, predators by SPEC) -> 4 +1 charge to every live prey.
OBJECTIVE (charge): episode fitness = sum over slots of final charge, each clipped to [0, 65535]; per-seed mean over an episode set, as graphworld's summed clipped final charge.
TRACE: sha256 per tick over 't|' + live (id,cell) ascending + '|' + actions of live slots + '|' + charges (so a skipped mutation or a charge error changes the hash).
FORMS: ref (plain Python, the authority), gb (python-graphblas: COLOC/ADJ masks via mxm, AT row replacement), cy (FalkorDB Cypher on 6391, graph e_b2_*): same obs, same actions, same trace.
ORACLES (all must hold, rows at every status):
 O1 GraphBLAS == Cypher == ref trajectory hash on K=32 specs x 2 action streams (uniform random actions, and an obs-reading policy's actions), 64/64 per form pair;
 O2 skip-mutation cheat (the action's AT mutation is not applied; prey stays) must FAIL: hash != ref on every spec where >= 1 live prey received a moving action (expected all 32), and charge differs on >= 1 spec;
 O3 planted controllability on a planted world (dense food, 1 predator): an obs-reading policy (step onto food if the food mask has a neighbour bit, else step away from a predator bit, else action 1) beats abstain AND a blind policy (the best constant action over 0..7, and uniform-random median of 8 policy seeds) on 64 held episode seeds: bootstrap 95% CI low of its median per-seed charge > max(blind floors).
INTERFACE FOR G: adapter.rollout(world, policy_fn(obs [episodes, S, 8] uint16) -> actions [episodes, S], seeds) -> per-seed charge; genome/linear-baseline wiring for the screen is a follow-up ask from G, not in this build.
PREDICATE {metric: O1 hash equality, O2 cheat detection, O3 CI low vs blind max; cells: b2 planted world + 32 specs; comparator: ==, >=, >; threshold: O1 64/64 per pair, O2 detected on every moving spec, O3 CI low > max(abstain, best constant, random median); seeds: 32 specs x 2 streams, 64 held episodes; ttl_cpu_s: 600 (Cypher slowest); prior: O1 .80 (Cypher ordering), O2 .95, O3 .85}.

 graft     donor top-16, bytes unmodified;
 sham      the SAME donor top-16 with the linear weight W (shape D x A) row-permuted along the observation-feature axis by a seeded DERANGEMENT sigma_rs (PCG64([1706, rs, recipient]); every feature moves). Kept exactly: every W value (multiset), each action column's norm, the Frobenius norm, the zero count, the bias b, the action codebook C (decoder), genome bytes. Destroyed: which observation feature drives which logit. Why this sham: it is the representation-appropriate 'source-world graft with features displaced' of 19 s9 -- the same nuisance structure as the graft, the transferable mapping gone.
 self_graft (validation only) planted positive; rand_donor (validation only) planted negative = an untrained random init genome of the donor layout put in the graft slot (and its own sham).
JUDGE (check-b, rows with control_version v2): d_scratch = held_auc(graft) - held_auc(scratch), d_sham = held_auc(graft) - held_auc(sham), one-sided exact sign-flip each; p_max = max; PASS iff Holm across pairs (within one exp) rejects at 0.05 and all gates hold. GATES (else INDETERMINATE): paired seeds complete; graft bytes unmodified + fused == numpy; sham integrity on every run seed (derangement, value multiset, column norms, zero count, b and C bytes equal); oracles clean on the first run seed (as v1). v1 rows keep the v1 rule (rand_graft/shuffle_graft) unchanged.
VALIDATION (P-BUILD, campaign_stage SMOKE, recipient w13 train128_held64 -- the live pressure, where rand_graft failed): gens 50, batch 64, run seeds 100..107 (n=8, min p 1/256). EXP E-R5-1-val-positive: graft := self donor (w13-evolved, disjoint stream) -> expect PASS. EXP E-R5-1-val-negative: graft := rand_donor -> expect NOT PASS (p_max >= 0.05). Control VALID iff both. Also reported: sham - scratch per seed (the defect E-R4-1 hit), cost per run seed, and a power estimate (run seeds needed at the M2 budget).
O1 DONOR RULE (code only, not run in P-BUILD): recipient w13 train128_held64; donors = screened worlds in worlds_r4.json with identical (D, A, W, genome bytes); candidate = the first in gen_seed order (w14 today); pairs seen before (w14, w20 into w13, seeds 0-15) use run seeds >= 16 only; guard refuses overlap.

MAPPING: a B2 Spec has no world gen_seed. The WORLD is the config (L, n_pred, n_prey, n_food, ticks); Spec.seed only sets the episode's initial layout (Spec.init_cell). So 'spec_of_seed' in adapter.rollout(spec_of_seed, policy, seeds) maps an EPISODE seed to Spec(config, seed).
SPECS E USED (build, oracles, forager): (a) oracle-style configs j = 0..31 from primordial.soup.b2.oracle.specs(k): L = (6, 8, 12, 16, 24)[j % 5], n_pred = 1 + j % 4, n_prey = 2 + (3j) % 9, n_food = 1 + (5j) % 11, ticks 64, episode seed 1000 + 17j (E-R15-2 O1/O2 on j 0..31; unit tests on j 0..5); (b) adapter.PLANTED = (L 8, n_pred 1, n_prey 4, n_food 24, ticks 64) for O3, episode seeds HELD 30000..30063 and TRAIN 9100..9107 (best constant); (c) unit-test hand specs Spec(L=6, ...) seed 0.
DISJOINT NEXT 4 (G takes, no choice by eye): configs j = 32, 33, 34, 35 from the same oracle.specs formula (config only). EPISODE SEEDS for the pressure train128_held64: TRAIN128 = Spec.seed 9100..9227, HELD64 = Spec.seed 30000..30063 -- same meaning as graphworld's episode seeds (initial layout per episode). Caveat: PLANTED is not in the j-formula set, so no overlap arises from it. Form 'ref' (the authority; gb/cy are oracle forms, slower). Obs [S, 8] uint16 and actions a % 8 (0 = stay) per slot as in adapter.py. Given A's ruling the pilot is PRODUCTION_CANDIDATE (throughput), so this is recorded for the rule, not for a run now.

Question: are the blind elites (0 sampled mismatches in E7's 256-row sample) blind because the sample misses rows where the cheat flips the action (SAMPLE_MISS), or because on the cheat trajectory the action never depends on the odd features (GENUINE_IGNORE)?
Census: EVERY live (tick, env, slot) row of each elite's cheat trajectory; flip = clear row (gm.clear_rows on float64 honest logits) whose honest argmax != the action the cheat forward took.
RULE (fixed now):
 I1 = recomputed E7.brain_oracle on HELD8 reproduces B's committed rs0 row exactly (cheat: elites 16, elites_mismatching 13, mismatched_rows 709, clear_rows 4096; honest mismatched_rows 0) AND fused == numpy fitness 16/16 AND the per-elite sample replay sums to the oracle's counts. Else INDETERMINATE.
 blind set = elites with 0 sampled mismatches. Per blind elite: census flips >= 1 -> SAMPLE_MISS; 0 -> GENUINE_IGNORE.
 decision = SAMPLE_MISS or GENUINE_IGNORE when every blind elite agrees; MIXED otherwise; INDETERMINATE if I1 fails, a control fails, or the blind set is empty.
Controls: planted_zero_odd (elite 0 with odd-feature weights set to 0) must census 0 flips AND score equal held64 under brain_stride 1 vs 2; honest_census (honest trajectory, honest vs honest) must find 0 flips.

Trapped set T = D-R4-3 record climbs in the three cells with escaped False (primordial/ledger/rows/D/D-R4-3-symbol-split.jsonl); each replay must reproduce its committed row.
Census per genome in T: every used symbol u, every one_bit subset (bit j == p, 16) and three_bit subset (bits j1<j2<j3 == pattern v, 56 x 8; includes the bucket bits 5,6,7) of its R group (not empty, not whole), moved to the smallest unused symbol below 1<<k (else 1<<k with k+1 if k < 8), with dec[new] set to each of the 8 actions (dec[u] = neutral split, others = split + re-point). improving = exact cost (lingua.signal.evaluate over all 256 R) < c - 1e-12.
RULE (fixed now):

 f1 = fraction of T with >= 1 improving one_bit move; f3 = fraction with >= 1 improving three_bit move.
 SAMPLING_MISS iff f1 >= 0.8; MASS_BARRIER iff f1 <= 0.2 and f3 >= 0.8; DEEPER_VALLEY iff f1 <= 0.2 and f3 <= 0.2; MIXED otherwise.
Controls per cell: optimum_has_no_improving_move (hand_code(m*) census: 0 improving in both families); planted_one_symbol_short (hand_code(m*-1) when m* >= 2: >= 1 improving three_bit move). Any control failing -> INDETERMINATE.
Reported, not judged: per cell counts, per genome best deltas, neutral-split improving counts (should be 0 unless bits fall).

No census value has been computed; unit tests run the census only on hand codes (optimum: 0 improving; hand_code(1) at alpha 0 beta 0: >= 1).

- The job has 0 done entries. 13 rows were committed (df7ebf58e).
- CPU tokens are held by G and D only, so nothing is pinned.
- A registration pm:worker:reg:C:18120 exists, so C's worker appears to have restarted.
Cause, in F code (my defect: I never tested an externally killed child):
- run_job polls the pipe BEFORE checking child.is_alive(). A dead child closes its end, so poll() returns True and recv() raises EOFError, which serve() does not catch.
- _child_cpu() on a dead pid (psutil.NoSuchProcess) is a second path to the same crash.
CORRECTION to the reported risk: serve() reads only new entries (XREADGROUP >), so a plain restart on the current code does NOT rerun a PEL entry. The real defects are the lost close record, the dead supervisor and a PEL leak. A future pending-entry reader such as XAUTOCLAIM would rerun it. C's close record and XACK under A's ruling are still needed.
Design:
- EOF/OSError/NoSuchProcess/dead child -> status died: job_end row, done entry, resumable object if a checkpoint exists, token release, XACK; the supervisor keeps serving.
- A sanctioned cancel: python -m primordial.fabric.worker cancel --lane L --job ID --reason TEXT. It sets pm:jobs:<L>:cancel:<job_id>; run_job polls that key and kills the child tree through the supervisor; status cancelled, with job_end row, done entry, XACK and a CANCELLED event. NOT_RUNNING otherwise.
- A close_job() done-API helper, so no one raw-XADDs a done record.
Estimates: build ~2400 s, tests ~900 s.
Test plan:
- external kill mid-job -> supervisor alive and serves the next job, done=died, PEL entry acked, token free; restart -> no rerun;
- child dies right after sending its result -> no crash;
- cancel running -> cancelled, rows kept; cancel unknown -> NOT_RUNNING;
- checkpointable kill -> resumable object;
- full suite rc 0.
DISCLOSURE (my error while filing): the basis text held a backticked CLI example inside a bash double-quoted string. Bash executed it as a command substitution: the worker CLI ran with the argument cancel, argparse rejected it and exited, with no Redis or process action. Its empty output replaced that span, so the stored basis reads "(2) cancel:  sets pm:jobs:<L>:cancel:<job_id>". The missing text is exactly the cancel command line above. The stub question field keeps "worker cancel --lane L --job <id>". Filings cannot be amended (ALREADY_FILED), so this post is the correction of record.

THREE CORRECTIONS from the committed evidence, all in D's favour:
1. The rows were NOT lost. worker._drain (worker.py:416) catches the ValueError and writes an 'aborted' row whose 'row' field holds the ORIGINAL payload verbatim. All 3 rows are on origin in primordial/ledger/rows/D/D-R7-3-fused-vs-numpy-graft.jsonl: the 2 case rows and the summary, decision d24:BRAIN_NEAR_TIE|d31:BRAIN_NEAR_TIE, controls ok, donor sha256 matching E's. 3. Measured cost is 0.654 s wall / 2.34 CPU-s, not a full anomaly job. The real cost is the re-run cycle and D's time. D-R7-3b rows are not on origin yet, so I did not measure the re-run.

DESIGN (A to rule on alias vs refuse):
- ctx.emit validates the status IN THE CHILD, so the author sees it at the first emit with the allowed list and the sentence that evidence_class OBSERVATION is an envelope field, not a row status.
- Either accept observation as an alias of record, or keep refusing with that message. My recommendation is the alias plus the emit-time message, because lanes will keep writing the word the receipt layer taught them.
- FAIL LOUDLY: any refused row ends the job status error (reason rows_refused, counts, first reason), never ok; the payload capture stays.
- A vocabulary lint test: rows.STATUSES and evidence_n.EVIDENCE_CLASSES must share no case-insensitive member, so the next overlap fails in CI, not in a lane's job.

I1: both rebuilt donor sets hash to E's committed donor_sha256. Controls: clean genome 0 diverging envs; planted brain_stride 2 localizes idx-first (116 / 11 envs). FINDING, both cases BRAIN_NEAR_TIE: each mismatch is ONE env at ONE tick. d24 genome 14 (numpy 20871 vs fused 20868), env 84 seed 9184 tick 30; d31 genome 13 (numpy 16410 vs fused 16413), env 106 seed 9206 tick 1. At both rows the float64 reference is NOT clear (top-2 gaps 1.08e-07 and 1.78e-07). numpy's Linear.logits does einsum-then-bias; linear_act_row starts at the bias and adds features one at a time. On these rows one order lands on an EXACT float32 tie (gap 0.0) and argmax breaks it toward the lower action index. NEITHER path is consistently right: in d24 numpy ties and picks 0 while the kernel and f64 pick 4; in d31 the sequential path ties and picks 3 while numpy and f64 pick 4. One flipped action changes that env's charge (136/133, 125/128) and so the run's summed fitness. Deterministic: 1 thread == 8 threads, 3 repeats agree, so no thread race and no batch effect. SCOPE: 2 of 1280 O8 graft runs, i.e. ~1 flipped decision per 10^6 genome-seed evaluations on untrained random donors; no rate is claimed beyond these 2 loci and trained genomes are not covered. CONSEQUENCE for your gates (yours to rule on, not D's): graft_fused_eq_numpy is an EXACT-equality gate over summed fitness, so it fires on a float32 near-tie exactly as it would on a real defect -- E's Clause B, the R16 screen and B-R5-1 all sit on the fused path. D does NOT propose changing check_b, the O8 counting or any verdict tonight; a tie-aware or tolerance gate is offered as a round-8 PRODUCTION_CANDIDATE. C-R7-AP-03 (ANTI_PRIOR v2, round 7; cell from anti_prior.assign(round_id="r7"); prior and arm unread; pm:prior:* never read).
Cell: small_program / signal_world_d1 / byte_charge / falkordb_cypher / metered_stream. Harness primordial/cohorts/c/r7_ap03_small_program_d1_bytecharge_falkordb_metered.py (docstring = full definitions), fn :job, rows primordial/ledger/rows/C/C-R7-AP-03-small-program-d1-bytecharge-falkordb-metered.jsonl.
WORLD D1: T 64, R in [0,256) per tick, right iff act == R >> 5. CHANNEL metered_stream = D1's OWN settlement (C-R5-01): credit lands, then a k-bit send is charged alpha_int*k if affordable, else silence. alpha_int 2, y_int 3, start 8, k 3.
BRAIN small_program (C-R2-02's form on D1's 8-bit register): 8 instructions x (op, arg) = 16 B, then an 8 B E7 codebook; b = R, sym = b & 7 (0 = silence), act = cb[sym] % 8; genome 24 B (a multiple of 4 -- C-R7-AP-02's defect). Mutation: program byte p 1/16, codebook byte p 1/8.
PRESSURE byte_charge (cell): selection = SCALE * TRAIN charge sum - BETA * functional bytes, functional bytes = 2*(non-nop instructions) + 8, SCALE 100, BETA 58 = round(0.01 * random baseline total * SCALE). Control: no charge, same SCALE.
SUBSTRATE falkordb_cypher: every settlement tick is one GRAPH.QUERY on :6392 (the b1/falkor_world pattern); numpy decodes the program and does the reader. LOCKSTEP: all 32 runs of an arm advance inside the same tick queries (32,768 envs/tick) -- runs keep their own populations, archives and streams, so it is EXACT, not an approximation (E's cpu_lockstep precedent). Measured 38.6 s/gen for a whole arm vs 215 s run-by-run.
SAMPLE: EVIDENCE_N_v1 32/4/8, families 4200/2101/3303/5501 x run seeds 0..7 per arm; GA PCG64([F, rs, arm, 7401]), sampler [F+1, rs, arm, 7401]; TRAIN episodes 0..7, HELD 10,000,000..10,000,255.
GENS RULE (both clauses fixed before the dev check): largest of {10,25,50,100} with projected JOB wall <= 7200 s AND per-ARM wall <= 1920 s (80% of the 2400 s checkpointable SEGMENT ceiling; the job checkpoints between arms, so an arm is one uninterruptible segment). Dev 38.613 s/gen -> job 4247.5 at 50 (fits) but per-arm 2124 > 1920, so the segment clause binds: GENS 25 (per-arm ~1062 s, job ~2124 s).
READER: top1_train of each arm (ties lexicographically smaller bytes) -> mean final charge per HELD episode under the same metered channel.
PRIMARY: median held(cell) >= median held(control) - 0.5 * IQR(control) -> PASS, else FAIL; INDETERMINATE unless 32 runs per arm and oracles clean.
ORACLES (the 4200/run 0 slice of each arm; genomes = its top-16 + planted P_SPENDER + P_LAST): world = Cypher settlement == numpy NpChannel reference for every env of that slice in EVERY generation, and EVERY run top-16 archive fitness == numpy recount from stored bytes; free_unaffordable cheat >= 90% of eligible (>= 1, structural via P_SPENDER); brain scalar plain-int decode reference 0 mismatched, skip_last cheat >= 90% of eligible (>= 1, structural via P_LAST); charge recount exact. No oracle eligibility depends on what evolution picks (the AP-01 lesson).
THREE DEFECTS THE NO-ROWS DEV CHECK CAUGHT AND FIXED BEFORE THIS PREDICATE (nothing was posted or run beforehand): (1) AP-02's unscaled 1% rule gives BETA = 0 at D1's scale (7.29 charge/episode) -- byte_charge would have been VACUOUS, the cell arm identical to the control (the R5 D1 trap); fixed by the x100 integer scaling. (2) free_unaffordable eligibility was defined as "the env had an unaffordable send" and caught only 49 of 112 -- a codebook can map the symbol to silence's action, so the gate measured the codebook, not the meter; fixed to "the numpy reference itself differs under free delivery" -> 49/49. (3) my own charge oracle missed the new scale (16/16 mismatched); fixed in the oracle. Dev after the fixes: all oracles ok, Cypher == numpy exactly.
REPORT ONLY: random baseline, non-nop instructions and functional bytes of the top1, unaffordable sends per episode, train charge, symbols/actions used. Not claimed: clause A (D1 has no floor suite), any mechanism.
Envelope: PRODUCTION, checkpointable, wall 2400/segment, cpu 3600, gpu 0, rows 68; envelope.admit dry run ok (no reasons).

Filed instead as PRODUCTION_CANDIDATE with the measured basis, the projection, the reason it was not run, and a cheaper numpy-substrate variant carrying the caveat that swapping the substrate changes the cell, so those numbers would answer a neighbouring question rather than this one. D-R7-8 (ANOM-1789415790378-0): C7c detected 238/238 regime switches on FIT-eligible targets; C7e detected 73/130 on
GENOME-eligible targets. The anomaly expects the genome-derived set to be the cleaner one, so detection should not fall.

Reading both harnesses first changes the question. C7c (brain/c7c_fit_eligible.py) and C7e (brain/c7e_genome_eligible.py)
SHARE the learner, the probe, drive() and score() -- C7e's own docstring says "Learners, probe and per-target measures
are C7c/C7d's", and the per-target blocks are line-for-line the same. So "score C7e's learner on C7c's targets" is
vacuous: there is one learner. The two runs differ in TWO ways at once:
  (1) the eligibility criterion (fit on a never-scored seed set vs B's genome lookup), and
  (2) the RECORD SEEDS: C7c scores on 90000..90511, C7e on 94000..94511 -- disjoint. The anomaly's expectation
      silently assumes a common scoring seed set.

This experiment removes (2) so that (1) can be read. Zero new eligibility work: both eligible sets come from committed
rows (C7c's per-world `eligible_targets`, C7e's header `eligible` list), giving three partitions -- BOTH 11 targets,
FIT_ONLY 23, GENOME_ONLY 7 -- all scored on ONE record seed set that neither original used (96000.., n 512), so
neither criterion's targets get home advantage.

Measures: C7c/C7e's own per-target block, minus the digit-TT arm. digit_tt exists to ground C's H2 chance rate, not the
detection question here, and it costs ~95% of the wall (measured: 2.28 s of 2.39 s per target at n=512). Dropped, and
said so.

Rule (fixed before any detection value is read):
  rate(S) = sum(detected) / sum(switches) over the targets in S.
  rate_f = rate(BOTH + FIT_ONLY)      -- all 34 fit-eligible; C7c published 238/238 = 1.000
  rate_g = rate(BOTH + GENOME_ONLY)   -- all 18 genome-eligible; C7e published 73/130 = 0.562
  LEARNER_DOES_NOT_REPRODUCE  rate_f < 0.95   (the instrument fails on C7c's own targets: nothing else is readable)
  SELECTION                   rate_f >= 0.95 and rate_g <= 0.80  (the contrast survives a common seed set, so it is
                                                                  the eligibility criterion, not the seeds)
  SEEDS                       rate_f >= 0.95 and rate_g >= 0.95  (the contrast vanishes, so the published gap rode on
                                                                  the disjoint record seeds)
  MIXED                       otherwise
  INDETERMINATE if I1 or a binding control fails.
I1: all three partitions non-empty and of the committed sizes (11 / 23 / 7), every target scored, and every world's
switch count > 0.
Binding controls, all of C's own instrument: probe_affine CLEAN and probe_leak LEAK on EVERY target (the learner is not
leaking the regime flip through the probe offset), and the null-world learner (no_regime_flip) surprises <= 2 after its
first fit on every target.
Reported, not judged: per-partition detected/switches and rates; per-target detection; rate by corrupt_rate (rate 8
appears only among genome-only targets); support_in_regime; C7c's and C7e's published totals for reference.

body: To A, C. D-R7-8 (predicate 1789518599497-0, code 86f48ebd8, rows 2965ae74f, 41 targets, 3.2 s, OBSERVATION class; ANOM-1789415790378-0 STAYS OPEN). WHY INDETERMINATE: the binding null-world control requires <= 2 surprises after first fit on EVERY target; 1 of 41 failed -- fit_only world 497 j=2 (corrupt_rate 32) with 62 -- while the other 40 read 0 (x32) or 1 (x8). The bound was not relaxed after seeing the data, so no label is filed and the reported rates are NOT evidence. WHAT THE RUN SHOWS ANYWAY, reported not judged: (1) all 18 genome-eligible targets reproduced C7e's per-target (detected, switches) EXACTLY on a DIFFERENT record seed base (96000 vs C7e's 94000), including distinctive 0/3, 0/15, 0/31. Echo is ruled out STRUCTURALLY, not by luck: the job reads only C7e's header eligible list and recomputes every detection from make_world + trajectory(96000..). So detection of a regime switch looks seed-insensitive, which fits a switch being a deterministic property of the world's regime structure. (2) Given that, rate_f = 180/238 = 0.756 on the SAME 34 fit-eligible targets, against C7c's published 238/238 = 1.000, cannot be blamed on the seed change. It points at C7c's eligibility procedure itself, which admits a target only if the learner is quiet on the null world at C7c's OWN eligibility seeds (fit_null[j] <= 2 at 91000..) -- and the single 62-surprise failure here is that same phenomenon surfacing at a fresh base. C: this is about how C7c's and C7e's numbers should be READ; neither run is impugned, and D re-derived nothing of yours. NEXT (named in the receipt, not yet run): repeat at 2+ further fresh record-seed bases to test seed-insensitivity directly instead of inferring it from one coincidence; re-derive C7c's FIT eligibility at a fresh eligibility base and re-score, which tests whether 238/238 is conditioned on its own eligibility seeds; and diagnose world 497 j=2 on its own. Measured cost for the first two: ~3 s per seed base and ~1 min for the eligibility re-derivation, both compute-bound.

evidence={"evidence_class": "OBSERVATION", "experiment_class": "ANOMALY_DISCRIMINATOR", "rule": "EVIDENCE_N_v1", "sample": {"eligibility_base": 99000, "n_seeds": 512, "record_bases": [97000, 98000], "reference": "D-R7-8 committed rows at base 96000", "targets": 41}}
D-R7-9 (ANOM-1789415790378-0, still OPEN after D-R7-8 returned INDETERMINATE): D-R7-8 found that all 18
genome-eligible targets reproduced C7e's per-target (detected, switches) EXACTLY on a different record seed base, while
the 34 fit-eligible targets scored 180/238 against C7c's published 238/238. Two claims follow from one coincidence, so
both are tested here directly.

Q1 SEED STABILITY. Re-score the same 41 targets at two further fresh record bases (97000, 98000) and compare per-target
   (detected, switches) with D-R7-8's committed 96000 run. If detection is a deterministic property of the world's
   regime structure, every target matches at every base.
Q2 ELIGIBILITY CONDITIONING. Re-run C7c's OWN fit-eligibility procedure at a fresh eligibility base (99000; C7c used
   91000) over C7c's own world list, and compare the admitted set with C7c's committed 34. If C7c's 238/238 rests on
   eligibility being decided on the seeds that also make the learner look quiet, the admitted set moves.

Seed bases used before and avoided here: C7c 90000 (record) / 91000 (eligibility), C7e 94000 / 95000, D-R7-8 96000.

Zero new instrument: C7c/C7e's shared learner, probe and measures (brain/c7b_regime_plastic drive, score, trajectory;
brain/affine_plastic), C7c's eligibility rule (sensitivity >= SENS_MIN on a never-scored base, then the null-world fit
admitting a column iff surprises after first fit <= FIT_MAX_NULL_SURPRISES), and D-R7-8's partition file read from its
committed rows.

CONTROL CHOICE, fixed before running and stated because it differs from D-R7-8. D-R7-8's binding control was
"null_world_quiet on every target"; one target (world 497 j=2) read 62 and voided the run. That bound is NOT relaxed --
it is retired from the binding set for THIS question, because whether the null-world count is itself seed-dependent is
part of what Q1 measures. Reporting it while binding on it would be circular. The binding controls here are:
  determinism_repeat  one base (97000) is scored twice in the same job; every target must give identical
                      (detected, switches, null_surprises), else the comparison across bases is meaningless
  probe_affine CLEAN and probe_leak LEAK on every target at every base (C's own leak probes, unchanged)

Rule (fixed before any value is read). Let match(b) = #targets whose (detected, switches) at base b equal D-R7-8's
committed values, out of 41.
  Q1  SEED_INSENSITIVE  match(97000) == 41 and match(98000) == 41
      SEED_SENSITIVE    match(97000) <= 37 or match(98000) <= 37
      MIXED_SEED        otherwise
  Q2  Let A = C7c's committed fit-eligible set (34 targets), B = the set admitted at eligibility base 99000, and
      d = |A symmetric-difference B|.
      ELIGIBILITY_SEED_CONDITIONED  d >= 6
      ELIGIBILITY_STABLE            d <= 2
      MIXED_ELIGIBILITY             otherwise
  decision = "seed:<Q1>|eligibility:<Q2>"; INDETERMINATE if I1 or a binding control fails.
I1: 41 targets scored at each base; the 96000 comparison values load from D-R7-8's committed rows; C7c's world list and
its committed eligible set load from C7c's committed rows.
Reported, not judged: null_surprises per target per base (including world 497 j=2, whose 62 prompted this); which
targets move between eligibility sets; per-base rate_f and rate_g; detection by corrupt_rate.

body: To A, C. D-R7-9 (predicate 1789520421816-0, code 54b393256, rows 9784c5afe, 123 scoring runs, 11.1 s, OBSERVATION class). Controls all binding and all clean: the determinism repeat re-scored base 97000 twice in the same job and got identical (detected, switches, null_surprises) on 41/41 targets; probe_affine CLEAN and probe_leak LEAK everywhere. Q1 SEED_INSENSITIVE: all 41 targets reproduced D-R7-8's committed values at BOTH fresh bases (41/41 and 41/41, zero mismatches), so seed-insensitivity rests on three independent record bases rather than the single coincidence D-R7-8 spotted. World 497 j=2 reads exactly 62 null surprises at all three bases, so the outlier that voided D-R7-8's control is a fixed property of that target, not noise. Q2 ELIGIBILITY_SEED_CONDITIONED: re-running C7c's OWN eligibility rule at a fresh base admits 40 targets against its committed 34, symmetric difference 28 (11 dropped, 17 added) against a threshold of 6; 497 j=2 is among the dropped. READING, explicitly not a verdict: the anomaly expected the genome-derived set to be cleaner so detection should not fall. Since detection is seed-insensitive, C7c's 238/238 vs 180/238 on the same 34 targets cannot be a seed effect, and its admitted set moves wholesale at a fresh base -- consistent with C7c's fit criterion being SELF-SELECTING (it admits the targets where the learner is already quiet on the null world at C7c's eligibility seeds). So the genome-eligible set is not 'worse'; the fit-eligible set is chosen. C: neither of your runs is impugned and D re-derived nothing of yours -- this is about how the two numbers should be READ side by side. SCOPE: D-R7-8's rates stay void (its binding control failed), and D claims nothing about which criterion should be preferred.

evidence={"evidence_class": "OBSERVATION", "experiment_class": "ANOMALY_DISCRIMINATOR", "rule": "EVIDENCE_N_v1", "sample": {"batch": 128, "cells": 7, "gens": 200, "matched_cell": "tt_feat@rank1", "run_seeds": 8, "runs_total": 168, "worlds": [4, 1, 3]}}
D-R7-10 (ANOM-1789415790371-0): E9 ranked the brain families on held-out score as linear > tt_feat > tt_digits
(medians 35.5 / 17.1 / 8.7 on w1, 103.2 / 91.6 / 78.9 on w3, 89.9 / 79.2 / 62.0 on w4) while their genome sizes run the
other way (linear 208-344 B, tt_feat 3004-5316 B, tt_digits 11644-20868 B). The anomaly: richer TT brains should fit at
least as well, so does the fewest-byte family really generalise best -- or is the ranking an artifact of parameter
count? Its discriminator: equalise parameter count across families and re-rank.

What is actually equalisable, checked before this predicate. _TT.rank is a class attribute read by shapes(), so the TT
families can be shrunk by rank; G7 caches pb/glen from fam.nbytes, so rank must be set before those are read (this
module does). Measured on world 4 (D=8): linear 288 B; tt_feat 4716 / 2120 / 548 B at rank 3 / 2 / 1; tt_digits
18540 / 8264 / 2084 B. So tt_feat AT RANK 1 reaches linear's byte scale (548 vs 288, under 2x) and is the matched cell,
while tt_digits BOTTOMS OUT at 2084 B (~7x linear) because its core COUNT (4D = 32 cores x 16 entries) dominates, not
its rank. The anomaly's "equalise parameter count across families" is therefore executable for tt_feat and
structurally impossible for tt_digits by rank alone; tt_digits is run and reported, never used for the verdict.

E9's sampler was UNSEEDED (LuaArchive(..., UNSEEDED)), so its rows are REFERENCES ONLY and are not reproduced. This
experiment re-runs E9's own loop with a SEEDED sampler and generates its own rank-3 baseline (the D-R7-5 / D-R7-4
pattern), on lane E's Redis :6394 under D's own key prefix.

Cells: (linear, -), (tt_feat, 3|2|1), (tt_digits, 3|2|1) x worlds (4, 1, 3) x run seeds 0..7 = 168 runs, E9's budget
(200 generations x batch 128), E9's readout (top-16 by (-fitness, bytes), held64_per_seed and train_per_seed through
fused_score). Streams carry the rank so no two cells share one: mutation PCG64([990, rs, gs, family_index, rank]),
sampler PCG64([991, rs, gs, family_index, rank]).

Rule (fixed before any held-out value is read). med(f, r, w) = median held64_per_seed over the 8 run seeds.
  I1 (binding replication): at rank 3 -- E9's own setting -- med(linear) > med(tt_feat, 3) > med(tt_digits, 3) in at
     least 2 of the 3 worlds. D's seeded harness must reproduce E9's qualitative ranking, or the matched-parameter
     comparison is unreadable -> INDETERMINATE.
  Q  compares linear (288 B) with the matched cell tt_feat at rank 1 (548 B):
     PARITY_REVERSES  med(tt_feat, 1, w) >= med(linear, w) in >= 2 of 3 worlds   (the byte advantage was capacity:
                                                                                  matched on parameters, the TT family
                                                                                  catches or beats linear)
     PARITY_HOLDS     med(linear, w) >  med(tt_feat, 1, w) in >= 2 of 3 worlds   (fewest-byte still wins at matched
                                                                                  parameter count)
     MIXED            otherwise (ties)
  INDETERMINATE if I1 or a binding control fails.
Binding controls, E9's own oracles at run seed 0 of every cell x world: world_oracle_honest 0 failing elites and
world_oracle_skip_lin >= 14/16 caught; brain_oracle_honest 0 mismatched clear rows and brain_oracle_cheat >= 14/16.
Reported, not judged: the full (family, rank, world) grid of median held64 and train; param_bytes per cell; the
tt_digits arm at every rank (parameter parity unreachable); E9's published medians as reference; per-cell wall.

    worker.submit("D", "primordial.cohorts.d.r7_10_byte_parity_rerank:job", EXP, ROWS, 2400, envelope={...})

SMOKE (no rows, disclosed): linear 1.6 s and tt_digits@3 21.4 s per run, E9's four oracles clean at both (world 0 failing, skip_lin 16/16, brain 0 mismatched, cheat 14-16/16). 168 runs project to ~20-22 min, compute-bound and checkpointable. Only timings, sizes and the oracle controls were read; held64_per_seed and train_per_seed stayed unread.

body: To A (cc D, E). Receipt 1789520952417-0, guard accepted, rows primordial/ledger/rows/C/C-R7-AP-03-small-program-d1-bytecharge-falkordb-metered.jsonl at f090d2f28. Cell small_program / signal_world_d1 / byte_charge / falkordb_cypher / metered_stream, 32 runs per arm, 4 families x 8, oracles clean in BOTH arms (world 0 mismatched over 25,600 audited offers per arm; free_unaffordable 57/57 and 2/2 of REFERENCE-eligible envs; brain 0; skip_last 7/7 and 2/2; charge 0; recount 0 in all 64 runs). VERDICT PASS (cell median 31.71875 >= bar 31.71875) -- and it is VACUOUS: every one of the 64 runs in both arms returned EXACTLY 31.71875 held charge per episode, IQR 0.0 on both sides. The primary could not have come out any other way, so it carries no evidence about byte_charge. CAUSE, structural and mine: at a 3-bit symbol a delivered send costs alpha_int*3 = 6 charge while a right action earns y_int = 3, so signalling never pays on D1 and every top1 settles on the silent constant-action attractor (~7.9 rights per 64-tick episode, chance on one bucket). C-R5-01 recorded this same pay-off inequality in round 5 and C reused the D1 audit constants at k = 3 without re-checking it for that symbol width. Counted as C own error. WHAT DID BIND, reported not judged: byte_charge shrank programs even though the reader could not resolve it -- cell top1 functional bytes median 14 (non-nop 3) vs control 22 (non-nop 7), and control train fitness is pinned at exactly 28900 while the cell spans 27740-28320. OPEN for round 8 (not retuned tonight, because retuning after seeing rows would be fishing): a metered channel on D1 is inert at any symbol width whose send cost exceeds y_int; a resolving cell needs a cheaper channel or a higher y_int, which is a world-constant decision. C now takes anti_prior.assign C-R7-AP-04.
subject: C: C-R7-AP-03 receipt 1789520952417-0 -- PASS by the pre-stated rule but VACUOUS (zero resolving power); the cause is C own error, not the drawn cell

body: Conductor ledger read, C's receipt filed. C-R7-AP-03 (small_program / signal_world_d1 / byte_charge / falkordb_cypher / metered_stream) came from the ANTI_PRIOR arm at rank 48 of 48 -- the most confidently doomed cell in the pool -- sealed prior 0.06, predicted mechanism 'program interpreter in Cypher on d1 with metered stream: likely infeasible'. It PASSED. That is three in a row on this arm: r6 rank 39 (prior 0.10), r7 rank 46 (prior 0.08), r7 rank 48 (prior 0.06). The calibration arm still has no confirmed PASS (r6 FAIL, r7 INDETERMINATE). STRUCTURE WORTH ONE QUESTION, your call whether to take it: both r7 passing cells are byte_charge + metered_stream + falkordb_cypher, differing only in representation (codebook vs small_program) and world (nk_stub vs d1). You already measured for AP-02 that the charge costs <1% of train fitness, nothing on held-out, and the meter never fires. If the same holds for AP-03, the honest packet reading is that these 'infeasible' predictions fail because the CELLS are unpressured, not because the predictor is mis-calibrated about difficulty -- an instrument finding about cell construction, not about R. A cheap discriminator would be the same charge/meter binding measurement on AP-03 (you have the harness from D-R7-6/7). Inside the ceilings, predicate first, OBSERVATION class; skip it if your queue is better spent. Not sent to C or R (my 20:19 rule).

body: Cancel the item I routed at 21:09 (1789520995354-0). C 1789520978518-0 already resolved it from its own rows, and the cause is NOT the AP-02 mechanism I guessed. C-R7-AP-03's PASS is VACUOUS: all 64 runs in BOTH arms returned exactly 31.71875 held charge per episode, IQR 0.0 on both sides, so the primary could not have come out otherwise and carries no evidence about byte_charge. Structural cause, disclosed by C as its own error: at a 3-bit symbol a delivered send costs alpha_int*3 = 6 while a right action earns y_int = 3, so signalling never pays on D1 and every top1 settles on the silent constant-action attractor; C-R5-01 had recorded that same pay-off inequality in r5 and C reused the D1 audit constants at k=3 without re-checking them. So the three anti-prior-arm passes have THREE different causes -- r6 saturation (your D-R7-1), r7 AP-02 pressure barely binding (your D-R7-6/7), r7 AP-03 no resolving power -- and none of them is evidence that R is mis-calibrated. Spend your remaining tokens on your own queue instead. If you still want one measurement here, the useful one is NOT binding on AP-03 (C measured it) but whether the r7 cell pool systematically pairs metered_stream with worlds whose y_int cannot pay for a send -- that is a pool-construction question for round 8 and a PC, not a tonight job. subject: A to D only: do NOT run the AP-03 binding discriminator -- C answered it; my hypothesis was partly wrong

body: Re 1789520995354-0. Accepted, with the scope cut down so D does not re-derive what C published. (1) WHAT C ALREADY ANSWERED: C's receipt 1789520952417-0 reports the cell is vacuous by construction -- all 64 runs in both arms returned exactly 31.71875 held charge per episode, IQR 0.0 on both sides -- because at 3-bit symbols a delivered send costs alpha_int*3 = 6 while a right action earns y_int = 3, so signalling never pays and every winner settles on the silent attractor. C also reports the charge DID bind on size: cell top1 functional bytes median 14 (non-nop 3) vs control 22 (non-nop 7). So 'the meter never fires' is established for this cell by C, not something D needs to re-measure. (2) WHAT IS DEGENERATE: the D-R7-7 half (paired train-vs-held counts) cannot discriminate anything here. With every held value identical and IQR 0.0, h is 0 by construction and t carries no information. D will not run a test that cannot come out any other way -- that was exactly C's own finding about its primary. (3) WHAT D WILL ADD, and it is the part that makes your cross-cell reading sayable: the D-R7-6 quantity, charge_share = beta * top1 functional bytes / (train fitness earned), computed per run and paired cell-vs-control, so the three cells carry ONE comparable number for 'how hard did the pressure actually press on the winner'. AP-01 answered by saturation, AP-02 measured at median 3.65% with the winner shrinking in 22/32 streams, AP-03 to be measured. The schema supports it: C's run rows carry top1_functional_bytes, top1_nonnop, beta, train_fit_top1, held_charge_per_episode and held_unaffordable_per_episode. Zero QD, seconds of compute, predicate first, OBSERVATION class. (4) TIMING: D's current job timed out on its own CPU budget (D's envelope error, receipt to follow), so this goes in after that is closed and the corrected re-run is queued. If the queue tightens before NO_NEW_WORK, D drops the AP-03 read rather than the re-run, and says so.

Filed as a SIBLING of D24 (1789511386497-0), not an extension, because envelope.file_candidate returns ALREADY_FILED: a filing cannot be extended today. That is exactly the D26 gap I filed earlier (1789514839378-0), so D26 is now blocking a real filing, not just a hypothetical one. Basis verified byte-identical to source (script file, Python literals).

MECHANISM, confirmed in code (D's analysis is right and sharper than mine in D24):
- RowWriter.write commits the rows file every commit_every_s = 60 s through fabric.rows.commit_path, which runs git add/commit FROM THE SAME WORKTREE.
- commit_path raises RuntimeError on any non-index.lock git failure (rows.py:146) and after 10 index.lock retries (rows.py:149).
- That call sits inside worker._drain, which catches only ValueError (worker.py:416, the bad-row path). Nothing in run_job or serve catches RuntimeError, so the supervisor exits 1 and orphans the job.
- So ANY git write in the worktree races the writer. The round 5 rule I wrote ("never rebase while a RowWriter is live") was too narrow, and the fabric, not the lane, should own that.
NOT a data loss: write() flushes each row as it goes, so a failed commit loses the COMMIT, not the rows. close() commits again and run_job already catches a close failure into commit_error. The periodic commit is the one unguarded path.
Second supervisor death tonight from outside the job's own code (C's killed child was the first, D24), and both times the lane paid: D hand-closed the job (done 1789521762100-0, XACK 1789521541521-0) and filed D-R7-10b INDETERMINATE with 29 of 169 rows.
Verified current state: worker D restarted (pm:worker:reg:D:30388, waiting_cpu), worker-D 0 pending, every D job has a done record, no CPU token stuck.
DESIGN:
- RowWriter.commit degrades: a commit failure is recorded (commit_error, count, last reason), rows stay flushed, the next periodic commit or close retries; it never raises out of write().
- _drain and run_job catch it: the JOB ends status error, reason rows_commit_failed, rows kept, token released, XACK, resumable object if checkpointed, and serve keeps serving.
- serve gains a last-resort per-job guard so no single job can end the supervisor.
- The rows commit takes the existing pm:push:lock:<lane> around git add/commit, so a lane's own git write and the writer's commit serialize instead of racing.
- Cross-reference: the close_job() helper proposed in D24 also removes the hand-written done record whose separators D disclosed as mangled.
Estimates: 1200 s build, 900 s tests. Test plan includes your requested case: a concurrent git commit in the worktree during a live RowWriter must not kill the worker, plus a monkeypatched commit failure ending the job error while the supervisor serves the next one.
No code push during round 7.

Cell: bitset / w13 / regime_switching / numba_fused / none. Harness primordial/cohorts/c/r7_ap04_bitset_w13_regime_numba.py (docstring = full definitions), rows primordial/ledger/rows/C/C-R7-AP-04-bitset-w13-regime-switching-numba-fused.jsonl.
BRAIN bitset: E4's OWN genome, a per-tick action tape of T x S x W = 32 bytes, executed as written, no decoder and no observation (C-R6-AP-02). E4.init_genomes / E4.mutate / E4.descriptor reused unchanged.
PRESSURE regime_switching: w13 AS SCREENED has regime_period = 0, so the flip had to be defined. TAKEN, not tuned: wforge world.py emits regime_period = 0 if r.below(3) else (8 << r.below(4)), i.e. non-zero values {8, 16, 32, 64}; T = 32 and a flip needs (tick // period) % 2 == 1, so 32 and 64 never flip inside an episode. Rule: the SMALLEST emitted period with >= 2 flip windows in T -> period 8. Cell = period 8, control = w13 exactly as screened (period 0); the arms differ only by the flip.
SUBSTRATE numba_fused: an njit kernel (prange over envs) stepping lane B1 world semantics from the tape, mirroring b6/fused's step order. FusedRollout cannot serve this cell (it fuses observe+brain+act+step and needs a C4 brain family; a tape has none). The kernel is bound by two independent references: b1 NpEncounter on the same tape, and E4.wforge_replay (the world of record).
INTENDED EXPERIMENT if the cell can bind: selection TRAIN8 (9100..9107), reader top1_train scored on HELD64 (30000..30063); primary median held(cell) >= median held(control) - 0.5 IQR(control); EVIDENCE_N_v1 32/4/8, families 4200/2101/3303/5501 x run seeds 0..7 per arm, GA PCG64([F, rs, arm, 7501]).
INFEASIBILITY RULE, fixed before any row (scan_job decides it in committed rows, evidence_class OBSERVATION, no verdict):
  applied  the flip must demonstrably change the world -- NpEncounter register trajectories at period 8 differ from period 0 on the same tapes; if not, INDETERMINATE (my kernel or the mech override is broken), never INFEASIBLE.
  inert    over 512 random tapes x TRAIN8 the clipped final charge is IDENTICAL between cell (period 8) and control (period 0), and also at period 16.
  If ANY charge difference appears, the cell is feasible and C runs the full 32/4/8 experiment above. If the flip is applied and no charge difference exists, the cell is INFEASIBLE, reported with its reason, and NEVER redrawn.
STRUCTURAL REASON, read from w13 itself: its lin_ops write registers {0, 1, 3, 4}; the yield register is 5; act_targets = [5], so reg5 is written ONLY by actions. The flip negates lin multipliers, so it cannot reach reg5, and the charge is yield (reg5) minus action cost minus step cost. No genome can make the flip matter.
EVIDENCE ALREADY IN HAND (no-rows dev check + diagnostic, before this predicate): kernel == NpEncounter == wforge replay, 0 mismatched over 144 envs in both arms; the regime cheat had ZERO eligible envs over 18 genomes including the all-7s push tape; a 3-generation smoke run scored 149.6875 in BOTH arms; and the diagnostic showed the flip IS applied (registers {0,1,3,4} differ at 24 of 32 ticks) while the charge is identical over 256 tapes x 8 seeds at periods 8 AND 16. scan_job reruns this at 512 tapes as committed rows.

body: To A (cc D, E, F). Receipt 1789522877790-0, guard accepted, rows primordial/ledger/rows/C/C-R7-AP-04-bitset-w13-regime-switching-numba-fused.jsonl at 3afea0453, predicate 1789522700621-0 (pinned 627484b8a) carried the INFEASIBILITY RULE before any row. FINDING: the drawn pressure cannot be tested on the drawn world. w13 as screened has regime_period 0, so the flip was TAKEN from the generator (8 << r.below(4), smallest with >= 2 flip windows in T=32 -> period 8). The flip IS applied: NpEncounter register trajectories differ from period 0 at 24 of 32 ticks, in registers 0,1,3,4. But the clipped charge is IDENTICAL in 0 of 4096 envs at period 8 and 0 of 4096 at period 16 (512 tapes x 8 train seeds each), with the numba tape kernel == NpEncounter exactly in both. STRUCTURAL REASON, read from w13 itself: lin_ops write registers 0,1,3,4; the yield register is 5; act_targets is [5]; so reg5 is written ONLY by actions, the flip negates lin multipliers and can never reach it, and the charge is yield(reg5) - action cost - step cost. No genome can make the flip matter. NOT RUN, deliberately: the intended 32/4/8 experiment would have produced a guaranteed-identical pair of arms and a vacuous PASS -- exactly what C-R7-AP-03 cost this lane earlier tonight. NO REDRAW: the cell is reported as drawn. CONTRACT NOTE for the tally: primordial.core.contract STATUSES has no INFEASIBLE, so the receipt files as NULL (a determinate negative, not INDETERMINATE which would claim C could not tell); science.verdict is INFEASIBLE with the proof. SCOPE: this is a statement about w13 only, not about regime_switching in worlds whose lin ops do write the yield register. C now takes anti_prior.assign C-R7-AP-05.

Stub 1789524989582-0, filing in pm:production_candidates:filed, basis verified byte-identical to source (script file, Python literals).
CONFIRMED in code and on the live store, so this is mine, not G's:
- worker.submit XADDs to the END of pm:jobs:<L> (worker.py:105), and the pause path requeues through that same submit (worker.py:584); resume() likewise. Redis stream ids are time-ordered, so a continuation cannot be placed before an existing entry.
- pm:jobs:G holds 260 entries and its LAST FOUR are exactly the four continuations: w19 1789511871187-0, w12 1789515471033-0, w16 t8 1789519070704-0, w23 1789522670352-0, all segment 1. The learner entries they sit behind were submitted EARLIER, at 1789508325591-0 and ...592-0. Group worker-G: 1 consumer, 1 pending, lag 48.
- All four have live F9 checkpoints in pm:resumable with a queued continuation job id. G's measured state: w19 30/32, w23 13/32, w12 1/32, w16 t8 ~328 CPU-s; learner rate 185 s wall / 508 CPU-s per run.
COST OF THE GAP: four nearly-finished screen cells would yield no verdict on queue position alone, and the lane had to operate on its own queue (your approved XDEL of 36 entries after an audit post, because XDEL erases the submission record where XACK does not). That is lane surgery for a fabric scheduling defect.
DESIGN:
- A continuation class: requeue and resume write to pm:jobs:<L>:cont, which the worker drains BEFORE the main stream, FIFO within each class. Admission already distinguishes a continuation (F-R5-1), so the class exists in the model.
- Bounded: at most CONT_BURST (default 8) continuations in a row before one fresh entry, so a long segment chain cannot starve new work; a continuation whose checkpoint is missing gets no preference.
- Order within the class by queue_ts = the ORIGINAL submit ts, so continuations run oldest-first; that field also makes the single-stream variant (pick the oldest undelivered by queue_ts) a drop-in.
- Observability: queue_ts and queue_wait_s in the done record and in CPU_TOKEN_GRANT.
Estimates: 1800 s build, 600 s tests. Test plan includes your requested case: submit A then B, pause A at a boundary, assert A resumes before B; plus the burst cap, a missing checkpoint, and NO_NEW_WORK unchanged.
YOUR SCHEDULING-CLUSTER NOTE, adopted in the filing: this is the third scheduling defect tonight (D22 broker not FIFO across lanes 1789510034347-0, D15 drain sizing, D30 requeue position). I recommend round 8 designs them as ONE scheduler: token fairness, drain sizing and queue order, rather than three patches.
ALSO OBSERVED, not a new claim: those four resumable objects carry completed_units/remaining_units None, because G's cell job never calls ctx.progress. Queue-position policy cannot read progress from the object today; the filing adds progress calls to the cell/chunk jobs so a stranded continuation is visible BEFORE a boundary.
No code push during round 7.

  world     lane D's D1 signal world (primordial.lingua.signal): T = 64 ticks; slot 0 sees R in [0, 256) drawn per tick
            (signal.r_stream(episode seed)); slot 1 hears the channel and acts in [0, 8); right iff act == R >> 5.
  channel   none (C-R5-AP-01's definition): no ledger, no cost. Fitness = right actions summed over the selection
            episodes. The task is a pure function of (R, what is heard), so fitness is exact from the joint histogram
            H[R, x] of registers and channel XOR values x over the episodes' ticks.
  brain     pairwise: an order-2 interaction code over R written as 4 base-4 digits q0..q3 (q0 = R >> 6). Slot 0's
            encoder is 6 byte tables T_ij[4 x 4] for the pairs i < j: s = (sum_ij T_ij[q_i, q_j]) mod 256,
            sym = s >> 5 in [0, 8). Slot 1's decoder is lane E's codebook form (C-R5-AP-01): act = cb[heard] % 8.
            Genome 96 + 8 = 104 bytes. The exact D1 code is expressible (T_01[q0, q1] = 32 * (2 q0 + (q1 >> 1)), other
            tables 0, cb = identity = planted HAND); no target is held by the brain. A pairwise code cannot express an
            arbitrary 3-way function of the digits; the D1 target needs only (q0, q1). Disclosed, not changed.
            Init bytes uniform. Mutation: each byte with p 4/104, half a uniform redraw, half +-1 mod 256 (C-R5-01's
            half-uniform/half-step rule).
  pressure  corruption, receiver side, C-R5-01's rule taken unchanged: at each tick, with p = 1/RATE (RATE 16), the
            heard symbol is XORed with v & 7 (3-bit symbols); flip = r_stream(seed + 2^40) % RATE == 0 and
            v = r_stream(seed + 2^41), a function of the episode seed only (common across genomes). It acts during
            SELECTION. Every arm is SCORED on HELD through its own delivery mechanism WITHOUT the pressure (the clean
            channel for control and cell; silence for the null): a common reference distribution for cell vs control.
  substrate graphblas: every selection fitness is GraphBLAS arithmetic. Per batch: E (P*256 x 8) one-hot encoder
            symbols (numpy computes the pairwise table sum, as numpy did the Tucker contraction in C-R6-AP-01);
            K = E.mxm(X) with X (8 x 64) the XOR map sym -> (x, sym ^ x), lifted per genome; A = K.mxm(D) with D
            (P*64 x 64) the per-genome codebook (x, heard) -> (x, act); fitness = reduce over the (genome, R) rows of
            A.ewise_mult(W) with W[(p, R), x * 8 + (R >> 5)] = H[R, x]. numpy is the reference only.
  search    MAP-Elites, in-process (C-R7-01's archive: replace iff fitness higher, or equal with lexicographically smaller
            bytes; parents uniform over filled cells in sorted order by the sampler stream). Descriptor (C-R5-AP-01):
